name: Linum
grown_as: Scarlet flax, a hardy annual. William's packet names it Linum usitatissimum, but that is the blue common flax; scarlet flax is Linum grandiflorum 'Rubrum'.
habit: A slender, upright, airy annual 30 to 45 cm, thin stems branching near the top, each branch ending in a flower.

leaf.arrangement: Alternate, evenly spaced up the stems
leaf.outline: Narrowly lance-shaped, 1.5 to 3 cm long and a few millimetres wide
leaf.veins: One to three faint parallel veins

flower.petals: Five, free, broad and rounded at the tip (wider at the outer end), overlapping
flower.centre: A small dark, almost black, eye with five stamens and five styles
flower.behind: Five narrow pointed green sepals, mostly hidden
flower.carried: Alone at the tips of the thin branches, in a loose open spray, facing up; each flower lasts a day, the petals dropping by afternoon

fruit: Round capsules about 6 to 8 mm with a short point, in ten segments, green ripening straw-coloured. Seeds flat, oval, pointed at one end, glossy brown, about 3 mm.
seedling: Two small oval, smooth, bluish seed leaves, then narrow pointed true leaves up a thin stem

bloom: five broad overlapping scarlet petals in a saucer
seed: flat oval glossy brown seeds pointed at one end
seedling: narrow true leaves up a thin stem
young: thin upright stems with many small narrow grey-green leaves
flower: slender airy stems with single scarlet flowers at the branch tips
seedhead: small round pointed capsules on the thin branch tips

look_alikes: Common flax (Linum usitatissimum) and perennial flax (L. perenne) have sky-blue flowers. Fairy flax (L. catharticum) is tiny and white with opposite leaves. Corn poppy has four petals and cut leaves.
